items.title: Google, Meta and TikTok sue California to block law protecting children from addiction risk
paragraphs: Google, Meta and TikTok have sued California to block enforcement of ⁠a new state law intended ⁠to limit the risk ​of addicting children under 16 to social media platforms.

The law, known as Assembly Bill 1709, prohibits such platforms from offering underage children “psychologically exploitative features” that could lead to compulsive use, such as providing ⁠personal recommendations and sending videos through autoplay features. It also requires the deletion of children’s accounts with those features.

In separate lawsuits on Wednesday, Google, Meta and TikTok said the law wrongly compels them to honor California’s preferred means of ⁠presenting content to children and substitutes the state’s judgment for that of parents.

They said the law violates the US constitution’s first amendment free speech ​protections, as well as Section 230 of the federal Communications Decency ‌Act, which broadly shields online platforms from ‌liability over user content.

The office of Rob Bonta, the California attorney general, who enforces the state’s laws and is the only defendant, said ‌on Thursday it was reviewing the lawsuits. “Our office is committed to defending California’s commonsense laws to protect kids online,” it added.
Google owns YouTube and is a unit of Alphabet, while Meta owns Facebook and Instagram. TikTok is a unit of China’s ByteDance.

Governor Gavin Newsom signed the law on 10 September, saying children’s safety should be central to any discussion about technology, and California “will not stand by while unregulated technology puts our children at risk”.
The law takes effect on 1 January 2027, unless a judge voids it or puts ‌it on hold.

“Parents are best positioned to make the right decisions for their families,” Jose Castaneda, a Google spokesperson, said on Thursday. “Overly broad laws like this actually break the systems we’ve built to help kids find high-quality, age-appropriate videos.”

In its ​lawsuit, Meta said California cannot override its editorial judgments about how to curate and display billions of posts, while leaving children free to spend unlimited time on other online platforms that offer similar services.
TikTok, meanwhile, said protected speech “cannot be suppressed solely to protect the young from ideas or images that a legislative body thinks unsuitable”.
Other critics also accused California of overreaching. The Electronic Frontier Foundation, a non-profit digital rights advocacy group, called the law “a massive ⁠privacy and free speech nightmare”.
Many US states regulate children’s access to social media. Countries ​around the world have similar restrictions, including a ​ban in Australia on social media for children ​under 16.

In August, Meta agreed to pay up to $18bn and limit teenagers’ use of Facebook and Instagram ​under agreements with nearly all US ‌states, which accused it ​of violating privacy and consumer protection ​laws.

In the aftermath of whistleblower revelations that showed Meta was aware of the way its platforms harmed teens, Meta launched a suite of teen safety tools aimed at giving parents more oversight. The company has previously tapped influencers to promote these features around the world as an alternative to social media bans or limitations similar to Australia’s.

Google has come under fire more recently over the use of its AI tools on school devices. On Thursday, parents in California filed a lawsuit against the company alleging their teen daughter made plans to end her life after multiple interactions with AI mode on Google Search. She had access to the AI mode through her school-issued Google Chromebook. The company was also recently forced to backtrack on its decision to cut off a school or classroom’s access to Google Search if teachers or administrators decided not to enable Google’s other AI features for schools.
Google filed its lawsuit in federal court in San Jose, California. Meta sued in San Francisco, and TikTok sued in Los Angeles.

The companies and Snapchat parent Snap still face thousands of lawsuits by individuals, school districts, municipalities and other government entities claiming they sought to addict children and caused a mental health crisis that resulted in such harms as anxiety, depression and suicide.

items.title: Perrier-Jouët and Iris van Herpen partnership celebrates “biological processes that shape life”
paragraphs: Champagne house Perrier-Jouët has unveiled a creative collection with designer Iris van Herpen that draws on art nouveau design, soundscapes and the “invisible forces that shape the natural world”.
As part of the partnership, Van Herpen created Symphonic Bloom, a sculptural piece crafted from silk and recycled 22-carat gold.

The collectable sculpture was designed to delicately twirl up the neck of a Perrier-Jouët Belle Époque 1988 jeroboam champagne bottle. According to Van Herpen, it reflects “the unseen” and represents hidden entities, such as sound and energy frequencies.

During the piece’s creation, the designer recorded soundscapes of Perrier-Jouët’s champagne vineyards, documenting acoustic patterns via cymatics – a technology that makes sound waves visible via sand or water. The sculpture’s patterns are based on such vibrations.
“In nature, there is a silent yet ever-present dance of frequencies, rhythms, and biological processes that continuously shape life,” Van Herpen explained.
“The world is not only visual but vibrational – woven together by invisible forces that connect all living things,” the designer added.
The nature-informed element of the sculpture’s craft connects to Perrier-Jouët’s experimental regenerative viticulture programme, which aims to sustainably restore soil health across its vineyards.
Since 2021, the initiative has been successfully undertaken across 40 per cent of its sites.
This mirrors Van Herpen’s sustainability ethos, with the designer incorporating recycled materials into her designs and using techniques to minimise waste as much as possible.
In keeping with its multidisciplinary theme, Symphonic Bloom was also created to reflect the layered flavours of Perrier-Jouët Belle Époque cuvées and how they develop with time.
Alongside the sculpture, Van Herpen also produced Symphonic Life, a collectable edition of a Perrier-Jouët Belle Époque 1999 magnum, adorned in the botanical motifs seen in Symphonic Bloom.

Completing the set of collaborative cuvees is a bespoke version of Perrier-Jouët Belle Epoque 2018 that comes with a reimagined bottle and gift box, made in collaboration with cellar master Séverine Frerson.

“Inspired by the designer’s interplay of materials including metal, wood, silk and velvet, the cuvée reveals notes of white flowers, poached pear and grapefruit, lifted by a delicate touch of white pepper and a fine, silky finish,” said Séverine of Perrier-Jouët Belle Epoque 2018.
Perrier-Jouët explained that the collaboration with Van Herpen is built on a shared philosophy that spotlights and advocates for nature as a source of “inspiration, creation and transformation”.

“Treating nature as a collaborator, Iris van Herpen is one of fashion’s most forward-thinking designers, with a practice that reveals the invisible beauty of living systems, translating organic forces, micro-rhythms and subterranean life into visible form,” said Axelle de Buffevant, creative director of Perrier-Jouët.
De Buffévent explained that the shared mindset also mirrors its connections with the art nouveau movement, with which it has a long-standing cultural and artistic affinity.

The design movement’s reference was also interpreted by Van Herpen across the whole collaboration, where the movements of American dancer Loïe Fuller were also used as a source of inspiration across the project.
Fuller’s movements were used in art nouveau lamp design by French sculptor Raoul Larche, which is part of Perrier-Jouët’s extensive French art nouveau collection at Maison Belle Époque in Épernay.
The creations were presented on 21 October for Perrier-Jouët’s Banquet of Nature at The Peninsula Paris, which combined champagne, art and gastronomy into an interactive sensory gathering.
The project will continue its international journey in Miami, Florida, for the city’s design week in December 2026, of which the brand has a longstanding history.
“For many years, Perrier-Jouët and Design Miami have shared a commitment to creativity, craftsmanship and contemporary culture,” the brand said.
Perrier-Jouët is a partner of the fair and last year launched its Design for Nature Award, of which Van Herpen was the first recipient.
This year, during Design Miami, a final collaborative sculptural piece will be revealed, created by Van Herpen as the winner of the award.
To learn more about the collaboration, visit Perrier-Jouët’s website.

items.title: Over 1,000 tonnes of sewage seen at landfill site
paragraphs: More than 1,000 tonnes of "sewage sludge" have been seen at a landfill site near Doncaster, according to an MP for the town.
Lee Pitcher said in a Facebook post he had been told the waste was being stored in "an uncovered stockpile" at the site in Finningley.
The Labour MP said he had been in contact with the Environment Agency (EA), which confirmed on Thursday that it had "set out a series of actions" for the site's operator following an inspection.
The landfill, located in a former quarry, is operated by Tetron Finningley Ltd, which has not previously responded when contacted for comment by the BBC.
Pitcher, who is the MP for Doncaster East and the Isle of Axholme, said EA officers visited the landfill on 9 October and, after he "chased" them for their findings, they responded on Tuesday.

He said the EA had told him that during the visit "approximately 1,000 tonnes of sewage sludge were observed being stored externally in an uncovered stockpile" and had "identified concerns regarding whether site activities were being undertaken in accordance with the operating techniques and management arrangements described within the approved documents".
Pitcher said the EA had given the landfill operator until 10 November to resolve the issue.
The MP said he had subsequently contacted the EA again about "potential asbestos disposal at the site, along with the air quality and environmental ramifications this could bring".

items.title: Ahead of China trip, White House says America's 'best interest' will drive foreign policy
paragraphs: Editor's note: This story was translated from the original VOA Mandarin article.

On Wednesday, the White House told the Voice of America (VOA) that President Donald Trump’s foreign policy decisions “have never been motivated by politics.” The U.S. president is going to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping in two weeks on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China — their third bilateral meeting this year.
Voters focused more on affordability and the war with Iran in midterm elections that brought Democratic victories. President Trump will deal with a new Congress in January led by Democrats.

Recently, Democrats have criticized the White House for its delay of a $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan, loosening restrictions on advanced chip sales to China, and the administration's refusal to confront Beijing over its continued support of Iran.
Will the changing political landscape on Capitol Hill add new dynamics to the interactions between the two leaders?

In an email responding to a request for comment from VOA on Wednesday, White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly stated: “President Trump’s foreign policy decisions have never been motivated by politics. The Commander-in-Chief will always act in the best interest of the American people and our national security.”

In an analysis piece published following the midterm elections, Credendo — a Brussels-based European credit insurance group specializing in trade credit and political risk insurance — observed that there is little disagreement between the two major U.S. parties regarding relations with China.

The article points out that both parties view Beijing as a potential adversary and threat, therefore both support a restrictive approach, including export controls on advanced technology and restrictions on Chinese investments into the U.S., while avoiding an escalation in trade tensions.
The article further notes that an overwhelming majority on both sides in Congress supports strengthening U.S.-Taiwan relations.

David Shedd, former acting director of the U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency, believes that a shared concern by both parties regarding the threat posed by China serves as a foundation for policy continuity.

“While there's never unanimous positions on every single issue about China, there certainly is a very strong bipartisan trend within the House as well as the Senate when it comes to the threats represented by China,” he said in a pre-election interview with VOA.
Shedd predicts that the president will continue to seek constructive engagement with China, while Congress will keep scrutinizing security threats.

On Wednesday, China Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning said that Beijing is ready to continue working with Washington. In response to a question at the regular press briefing, she described the U.S. midterm elections as “a domestic affair” and stated that “China stands ready to continue working with the U.S. to uphold and deliver on the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state.”
Experts are assessing how the midterm election results could affect the Trump administration’s ability to deal with China.

Alicia Garcia-Herrero, chief economist for the Asia-Pacific region at the French investment bank Natixis, told Reuters, that the newly empowered Democrats could try to limit Trump's maneuvering power. "Democrats are unlikely to give Trump free rein on deals with Beijing," she said.

However, Jon Czin, a fellow at the Brookings Institution and former director for China affairs at the White House National Security Council, says when it comes to Washington’s China policy directions, while Congress may exert greater pressure and advance relevant bills, it is the president who remains in the driver’s seat.
"I don't think there will be big fluctuations in U.S.-China policy." said Czin in a pre-election interview with VOA.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that he learned as a former U.S. senator that a new Congress cannot change foreign policies that the president was elected to carry out.

“To my great frustration, when I was a member of the Senate, I realized that while there are things we could do, ultimately the foreign policy decisions are made by the Executive Branch,” Rubio said last Friday. “Congress plays a role. There’s no doubt about it. But the central role belongs to the Executive Branch.”
After Tuesday’s midterm elections, President Trump has emphasized "one of the stronger powers that a President has" — veto power.
VOA Mandarin’s Yu-wen Cheng and Lin Feng contributed to this report.

paragraphs: A lighting range comprising repeatable spherical and pyramidal forms made from delicate glass is among recent products published on our furniture directory.
Fragile lighting collection by Jaume Ramírez for Marset
A simple table lamp, created by designer Jaume Ramírez for Marset, comprising a round base and pointed shade, has been spun out into a larger lighting range using the same visual language.
Fragile is now a full collection spanning table, wall and pendant lights of varying scales, providing elegant lighting solutions for spaces of all sizes.
Other products featured on Dezeen Showroom recently include playful task chairs with pop-coloured bases and a modular furnishing system designed to zone open-plan offices.
Read on to find out about some of our latest products:
Flora armchair by Andreas Engesvik for Fogia

This dining chair is the result of a three-way collaboration between Swedish brand Fogia, designer Andreas Engesvik and Michelin three-star chef Esben Holmboe Bang, who works out of Oslo restaurant Maaemo.
Flora‘s cantilevered arms, padded backrest, thickly upholstered seat and slender frame aim to make users as comfortable as possible, providing the stamina for hours of seated conversation and dining.
Flora armchair by Andreas Engesvik for Fogia

Named ingCloud, the chair was designed to facilitate easy movement rather than perfect, rigid posture across the course of a working day.

items.title: Paraguay’s president quits after millions of people’s savings frozen in bank crisis
paragraphs: Paraguay’s rightwing president, Santiago Peña, resigned on Thursday after a political and financial crisis collapsed the South American country’s banking system in recent days.

At the centre of the crisis is Ueno Bank, which in just a few years under Peña went from an obscure digital bank to one of the country’s largest lenders, claiming to have about 60% of Paraguay’s adult population as customers.

Last Monday, the central bank ordered Ueno into resolution over insolvency, freezing the deposits of 3 million customers, leaving hundreds of thousands of families without access to money for food and basic daily expenses. Bank executives were arrested, and people took to the streets in massive protests.
In power since August 2023 and with a term running until 2028, the 47-year-old economist was already facing impeachment proceedings that had broad support.

“Dear compatriots, today I address you at one of the most difficult moments of my life. With my heart set on Paraguay and with the conviction that our republic must always come before any person or circumstance, I have decided to submit my resignation as president of the republic,” said Peña in a video.

Ueno Bank began as a finance company in the 1970s and, in 2021, was bought by Grupo Vázquez, one of Paraguay’s largest business and industrial conglomerates. At the end of 2023, it received authorisation from the central bank, already under Peña’s administration, to operate as a digital bank.

The bank rapidly expanded its operations, attracting customers with generous cash-back offers on groceries and sponsoring Paraguay’s national football team. On Wednesday, the players released a letter “demanding” a “forceful response” from the government and the justice system.

The bank came to manage between $800m and $850m in deposits from state and pension entities, including retirement funds, prompting criticism over conflicts of interest because of Peña’s previous shareholding ties to Ueno Holding.

Peña said that, as an economist, he had merely made an “investment”, but that he had already disposed of all his shares. When the local press pointed to possible improper favouritism in directing state and pension funds to the bank, he called it a “false media campaign” aimed at weakening his government.

On Wednesday, opposition lawmakers and even members of Peña’s Colorado party filed an impeachment motion holding the president responsible for the collapse. He had been a shareholder in the group that ran the bank until early last year and, in recent months, had reportedly been ignoring warnings from the central bank and the media about its operations.
Political pressure intensified on Thursday morning when the ex-president Horacio Cartes, his former ally, posted a message endorsing the impeachment.

“We will not stand on the side of the theft of public, private and pensioners’ funds. We must think of the people and of the values we uphold in the Colorado party. We support the impeachment of the president of the republic, Santiago Peña, in order to restore the institutional order of the republic,” he wrote.
Other lawmakers followed suit and began debating impeachment when Peña released a video announcing his resignation.
“I do so thinking of the stability of our country, social peace and the need to preserve our democratic institutions,” said the now former president.

“I also want to apologise to the people if at any point I failed them … But today my priority is only one thing: the peace of mind of Paraguayans who trusted their savings to our financial system … My greatest wish is that the return of those funds is guaranteed,” he added.
Since the scandal broke, Peña has insisted in interviews and statements that he committed no wrongdoing.

Opposition senator Rafael Filizzola called the case “the biggest fraud carried out from political power in the democratic era … This is a bank created from political power, to use public money for private businesses linked to political power, with the president of the republic at the head of it,” he told 1020 AM radio.

Peña, a former finance minister who promised to rebuild a “great Paraguay”, was a key ally of the US president, Donald Trump, in the region – one of the few Latin American presidents to attend Trump’s second inauguration. US officials, including the secretary of state, Marco Rubio, repeatedly praised him as a “strategic partner”, and Peña recently flew to Washington to discuss critical minerals and economic cooperation. Neither Rubio nor Trump has yet commented on Peña’s resignation.

It is still unclear who will replace him or when, because his resignation must, in theory, be accepted by Congress – in which case the vice-president, Pedro Alliana, would take over. Alliana is also suspected of involvement in the Ueno Bank scandal, which he has denied.

About an hour after Peña’s announcement, the lower house unanimously approved the impeachment motion, which now goes to the senate. If approved, even after his resignation, he would lose his senate seat and, with it, parliamentary immunity, leaving him to face any criminal proceedings in the ordinary courts.

items.title: Studio Shea designs South Carolina library as "community living room"
paragraphs: Brooklyn-based practice Studio Shea has completed a metal-clad library with a central atrium that draws on the civic and industrial context of its site in South Carolina, USA.
Clinton Public Library serves a railroad junction town of less than 8,000 residents.

The 11,000-square-foot (1,021-square metre) library translates the vernacular porch feature as well as the town’s agricultural and textile manufacturing heritage into a contemporary public building, Justin Shea, founder of Studio Shea, told Dezeen.
“At its core, the project was conceived as a welcoming community living room,” Shea said.
Set on 1.25 acres, the building’s scale and massing respond to its surrounding residential context in view of the town’s downtown corridor.

“The deep roof overhang creates a shaded front porch that recalls the familiar social role of the porch as a place for gathering,” Shea said, explaining that the low-pitched roofs and striated standing-seam metal cladding are a subtle nod to the area’s material character.
“Together, these elements give the library a contemporary identity while maintaining a clear connection to the character and history of Clinton.”
Inside, the library centres around a daylit atrium that is both the social and organisational heart of the program spaces and collections.
From the entrance, library patrons can see through the atrium to the collections, study areas, activity spaces and reading garden in a clear, easy-to-navigate scheme.
“Particular attention was given to the quality of natural light,” said Shea.

“A continuous clerestory draws soft, even daylight deep into the building, activating the interior throughout the day. At night, the illuminated atrium reverses that relationship, allowing the library to glow outward as a beacon for the community.”

The plan was designed for adaptability and flexibility, with the makerspace, children’s room, and meeting areas expanding into the center for larger workshops and the community room connecting with the lobby, service spaces and exterior plaza for after-hours events.

Inside, pops of colour, monochromatic spaces and varied textures create a playful environment suited to a broad range of ages and activities, while generous glazing contributes to the sense of openness.

A key element of the design is a community bench along the building’s exterior – designed by Studio Shea and fabricated with oak trees from the site by Piedmont Technical College – that ties into the lobby bench, circulation desk and collection shelving.
“What might otherwise have been an incidental site resource became a tangible expression of local participation and investment,” Shea explained.
“Public architecture can create a stronger sense of ownership when the community is given opportunities to participate in its creation,” he continued.
“A civic building does not need to be monumental to be significant; it can achieve meaning through being welcoming, useful, adaptable and genuinely connected to the people and place it serves.”

Other public buildings recently completed in South Carolina include a county administration building with “crisp edges” by Foster + Partners, the International African American Museum that floats above water by Pei Cobb Freed & Partners and Moody Nolan and a seaside restaurant designed for nostalgia by SDCO and Basic Projects.

items.title: Shares in Musk's SpaceX plunge as tech and AI stocks fall
paragraphs: Shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX have plunged as tech and artificial intelligence stocks more broadly plummeted a day after the Democrats swept to victory in the midterms.
Those losses dragged the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite stock index down, which had fallen by more than 5% at one point in early trading.
The market has been reacting to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the artificial intelligence (AI) industry following Democrat wins in key data centre states including Texas.
Following the election, some tech leaders have acknowledged they need to improve their communication around data centres and the benefits of AI.
SpaceX shares were down more than 9% in by lunchtime in Thursday trading, while Tesla shares dropped more than 11%.

Musk had spent nearly $450m backing Republican campaigns, including at least $45m in support of Ken Paxton for the Texas senate seat, but Texas was turned blue in the Democratic tsunami on Tuesday night.
Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned heavily against data centres, pledging a moratorium on new construction in the sector.
Shares in chipmakers have been suffering, with AMD dropping more than 14% on Thursday, while Micron shares had dropped by as much as 17% before recovering slightly.
Intel shares are down by more than 7% and shares in Nvidia have fallen nearly 9%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had fallen by 10%.
The stock falls also hit the S&P 500 index, which dropped by 3.8% by lunchtime.
Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said the steep sell-off on the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 was sending shockwaves into other markets.
"Fresh panic over the AI trade has hit Wall Street hard," she said.

"Fears that the vast sums poured into AI infrastructure may not deliver the returns investors have been banking on are now colliding with the prospect of a sharp slowdown in data centre construction."
Some tech leaders have said they were caught off guard by the backlash against data centres in the midterms.
OpenAI president and co-founder Greg Brockman said he believed everyone had been surprised by the reaction to data centres, and more work needed to be done to ensure communities were on board.

"A lot of our shift over the course of this year has really been to realise that from San Francisco trying to build infrastructure in Texas, Georgia, and other places, you can't just tweet and say: 'This is going to be good.' You need to be in those communities," Brockman said at the WSJ Tech conference in Napa, California on Wednesday evening.
Meta's president Dina Powell McCormick agreed that the industry needed to improve their communication about the benefits of AI.
"I think we need to double and triple down on telling the story," she told the WSJ conference.
Alongside the immediate impacts of the US mid-term elections, some investors have become concerned that AI shares could be in a bubble that is due a correction.

items.title: Duchess of Sussex’s estranged half-brother ‘person of interest’ in child sexual abuse inquiry
paragraphs: The Duchess of Sussex’s estranged half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, has been named as a “person of interest” in the Philippine authorities’ inquiry into child sexual abuse image allegations made against her father, Thomas Markle Sr.
The country’s interior and local government secretary, Jonvic Remulla, told a press conference in Manila there were “signs that point that the son is involved in the crime as well”.

He added that Markle Jr, 60, who alerted local police and the FBI to images he found in his father’s belongings, was not yet being treated as a suspect. His alleged involvement is not thought to be directly linked to the material he handed to the police.
More than 7,000 photos and one video – all of under-age males and females of Asian, Latin and European descent, with some as young as 10 and 11 – were uncovered, Remulla said.
He described the images as “the most deplorable displays of impunity towards sexual activity that I have ever seen”.
Markle Sr, 82, who is estranged from Meghan, has reportedly been moved into a care home for dementia patients in the US where he is now living.
Remulla said: “We’re determining if [the] son is involved … There are signs that point that the son is involved in the crime as well but only as a person of interest so far.”
He added: “We will know in the next few days.”

Markle Sr, who returned to the US from the Philippines in May, has admitted paying for sex in the Philippines but he has strongly denied possessing child abuse imagery, and suggested he had been “set up”. His son remains in Cebu City in the Philippines.
Remulla has previously described Markle Sr as “a possible sex offender of the grossest kind”.
Markle Jr reported his father after claiming to have found four storage boxes at his father’s home in the Philippines containing “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sex abuse images.

Police and FBI agents have since been investigating whether Markle Sr was in possession of any illegal images while living in the Philippines and in Mexico, where he previously lived, and where other illegal images were reportedly found in one of his storage units.

Markle Jr was recently interviewed at his home in Cordova, Cebu, as part of an international, multi-agency meeting via Microsoft Teams, according to the Sun, which first published the claims. He gave his statement to an FBI agent based in Florida, who specialises in child sex abuse cases.

In a statement issued when the allegations against her father were first published, Meghan said she was “deeply distressed” by the claims. She said she had been informed of disturbing allegations against her father in 2018 and had kept him from having contact with her children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, to protect them.

items.title: K-pop group NewJeans’s contract omitted rights to ‘sleep and free choice’ – report
paragraphs: The superstar K-pop group NewJeans signed restrictive record label contracts that waived their right to “sleep, rest and free choice”.
A new report from the New York Times found that the contracts were signed when the members of the record-breaking girl group were aged 14 to 17.

The contracts banned the performers from having an “insincere attitude” and engaging in “inappropriate romantic relationships”. They also struck standard child protection language which protected “basic human rights” including the group members’ right to education.

The contracts from record label Ador (a subsidiary of Hybe, home of popular groups BTS and Katseye) additionally excluded portions of the Korean government’s K-pop contract template stipulating that the label “shall not demand that a performer who is a minor engage in excessive physical exposure or overly sexually suggestive expression”.
In a statement to the New York Times, Hybe representatives said the company adheres to child-protection laws and works hard to make sure its artists work and train in safe conditions.

NewJeans are one of the decade’s most popular K-pop acts. In 2023, the five-member group followed Blackpink to become the second Korean girl-group to score a number one album on the Billboard charts. In November 2024, the band made global headlines when they announced their decision to leave the label amid contract disputes and claims that Ador had deliberately undermined their careers.
Band member Hanni alleged that NewJeans were mistreated by the label and accused Ador of “deliberate miscommunications and manipulation” in a statement to South Korea’s parliament last year.

Ador has consistently maintained that they did not violate their duty. “A unilateral claim that trust has been broken does not constitute valid grounds for termination of a contract,” the label said in a statement.
The label sued band member Danielle, a member of her family and the band’s producer in December 2025 for a total of nearly $30m for damages and a contract break penalty.
Hybe representatives told the New York Times that its exit penalty fees do not exceed industry standards.
In July, the group promised that 2026 would be the “summer of NewJeans,” with a teaser showing the group as a four-piece sans Danielle. New music has yet to emerge.
The new reports expose the shadowy world of K-pop contracts and shine a light on the restrictive conditions that the genre’s biggest stars can be subject to.

By the time they signed their contracts, the NewJeans members – Minji, Hanni, Haerin, Hyein and Danielle – had already clocked in years of training in K-pop “boot camps” which taught vocal training, choreography and foreign language education.
Schedules were strict, one source told the New York Times, and it was not unusual for rehearsals to stretch as late as 2am. NewJeans’s youngest member, Hyein, was 12 at the time.

After the band members received their exclusive contracts with Ador in January 2022, the parents of one member requested multiple changes. They were told that the “contract itself” could be reconsidered if it was not signed in its current form.
In a statement to the New York Times, Hybe said its contracts were legal and negotiated in good faith, with protections in place for the artist as well as the label’s investment in them.

That contract also struck government language that forbade performers working for “excessive periods of time”. It also stipulated that the band would have to repay a significant percentage of the plastic surgery costs that are common in K-pop.
“We do not even recommend cosmetic surgery or procedures against an individual’s wishes,” Hybe said in a statement.

The NewJeans contact also granted Ador rights to use the band members’ “name, photographs, likeness, handwriting, voice and any other elements” in perpetuity, in a level of ownership that goes further than government recommendations for such rights to end at the point of contract termination.
The clause also grants Ador the right to use the NewJeans members as AI chatbots or clones.
The Guardian has reached out to Hybe for comment.

items.title: Financial crime watchdog keeps North Korea on blacklist, urges countermeasures
paragraphs: Editor's note: This story was translated from the original VOA Korean article.
A leading financial crime watchdog, The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), has kept North Korea on its list of high-risk countries for the 16th consecutive year.

In the latest update of its "call for action" list, the FATF is urging countries to apply countermeasures, its strongest level of action, citing Pyongyang’s continued efforts to finance its weapons programs. Iran is the only other country subject to the "countermeasures" designation.
The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) announced the decision in a statement dated October 30 following its plenary meeting in Paris.

The FATF said it remains concerned by North Korea’s “failure to address the significant deficiencies” in its systems to fight money laundering and terrorist financing, and by the “serious threats” posed by its illicit weapons-related activities.

The U.S. Justice Department said, in a statement released last month, that North Korean IT workers had used stolen or fabricated identities to obtain remote jobs at more than 70 U.S. companies, generating approximately $3 million in revenue.

According to the department, the workers relied on U.S.-based facilitators who received and hosted company-issued computers at their residences, allowing the North Koreans to access corporate networks remotely while appearing to work from within the United States. The earnings are believed to have been transferred to North Korean-controlled entities subject to U.S. sanctions.

The FATF called on countries to maintain countermeasures against North Korea, including cutting ties with North Korean banks, shut down closing their branches and subsidiaries, and limit dealings with North Korean people and companies.

The watchdog also expressed concern that North Korea has “increased its connectivity with the international financial system”, potentially heightening the risk of financing the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.

It said Pyongyang frequently uses “front companies, shell companies, joint ventures and complex, opaque ownership structures” to evade sanctions, urging countries to exercise enhanced due diligence on transactions conducted on behalf of North Korean entities.

The organization also noted that the termination of the U.N. Security Council's Panel of Experts on North Korea has made it more difficult to obtain reliable information needed to assess proliferation financing risks.
Russia vetoed a resolution to extend the panel's mandate in 2024, effectively ending its work.
The FATF's latest assessment comes amid continued concerns over North Korea's use of overseas networks to generate revenue and circumvent sanctions.
The FATF, established in 1989, sets international standards to combat money laundering, terrorist financing and the financing of weapons proliferation.

Its high-risk list, commonly referred to as the “blacklist,” currently includes North Korea and Iran. Myanmar is also listed and the FATF is recommending enhanced due diligence in dealings with the country.

items.title: “If we loved him, we had a movie”: the directors who had to make the Cat in the Hat likeable
paragraphs: Turning a Dr Seuss illustration into a fully realised 3D world is harder than it sounds, and directors Alessandro Carloni and Erica Rivinoja knew what they wanted to avoid on Warner Bros. Pictures Animation’s new The Cat in the Hat movie: CG that simply imitates a picture book.

“We didn’t want to use CG to just ‘simulate’ an illustration,” Carloni says of making the new 2026 animated movie. The aim was for audiences to feel the familiarity of Seuss’s painterly illustrations while experiencing the depth and immersion of modern 3D animation.

The creative partnership behind the film was just as collaborative. Asked how they divided the writing and directing duties, Rivinoja says they didn't split the work between them. “It was less ‘divide and conquer’, and more ‘unite and conquer’. To streamline the process, we were usually in meetings together.”

Working with Autodesk software such as Maya and Flow was key, as revealed in a new video series called Made to Make, which has now been expanded to include more behind-the-scenes details; watch it on the Made to Make YouTube channel.

Put simply-ish, it meant rethinking lighting, surfaces and even the edges of objects. The team paired simple, almost flat surfaces and key lighting with softer, more volumetric fill and bounce lighting. They also developed a stylised, painterly edge treatment to avoid the harsh sharpness of digital imagery. Then came realistic lens behaviour, including halation, aberration, and lens flare, which Carloni says helped ground the images in believability. The team developed the combination specifically for the film, creating its own visual style.

Maya sat at the pipeline's centre. Production designer Aidan Sugano’s hand-drawn designs were translated into 3D models there, and everything in the film, from characters and props to entire worlds, was built in the software.

For the animators, Maya was also the only way to touch the characters. Marek Kochout, for example, shaped the Cat’s performance through the Graph Editor, where a single expressive shot can involve hundreds of layered curves. The Pose Library let animators save and reuse expressions and attitudes, and over time it became a shared reference for how the Cat moves, with standout scenes added so every animator could draw on them.

Keeping a film like this on track across four countries, with teams in India, Montreal, London and Los Angeles, fell to Autodesk Flow Production Tracking, which followed every character, environment, prop and version from boards through to final compositing over roughly two years. Sugano, in New York, and VFX supervisor Matt Waters, in London, used RV within Flow Production Tracking to review the same footage in real time. Executives and partners screened the film through PIX, now part of Autodesk Flow Capture, whose watermarking and access controls helped keep it under wraps. As Carloni puts it, “This movie would not exist without the tools we had.”
For a fuller look at the workflow, visit Autodesk’s blog on the making of the film.

For Rivinoja, preserving Seuss's visual language was essential. The team wanted fans to recognise his signature design motifs, from hatch marks and negative space to his colour palettes, arches and mechanical hands. “We wanted to make sure people who love the books saw something of the book in the film,” she says.

It wasn't going to be a straightforward page-to-screen adaptation, though. The filmmakers wanted to expand the world and make it a cinematic spectacle, exploring what happens after the original story ends, including where the Cat goes when he leaves the house. They came up with the idea that entertaining bored children is his job, which explains why he shows up at the house on a rainy day. He's also one of many specialists at the company, and his famous hat is actually his company uniform.

The film also needed several distinct environments: the real world, Seuss’s world and three further worlds connected to characters in the story. Rather than altering the characters to suit each setting, the team kept their designs and shape language consistent.
“We kept consistent shape language throughout, and we didn’t change the looks of the characters,” says Rivinoja.
The differences come from colour, surfacing, rendering style and lighting, Carloni explains. The characters stay recognisable while the emotional feel of each world changes as the story progresses.

Carloni says the hardest problem was making sure audiences would want to spend time with the Cat, explaining: “To make sure the character of the Cat was truly lovable. The kind of character anyone would want to spend time with. If we loved him, we had a movie. If he's unlikable, then no matter how fun the story or how fantastic the adventure, the movie would never work.”

He describes animation's greatest advantage as the same thing that makes it daunting: ultimate freedom. “There are limitless possibilities. You can literally do anything at all in animation. As the saying goes, the only limit is your imagination, which makes it perfect to tell a Seuss story and create a Seuss world.”
The Cat in the Hat arrives in cinemas and IMAX in North America on 6 November 2026, with international releases beginning on 4 November.

Ian Dean is Editor, Digital Arts & 3D at Creative Bloq, and the former editor of many leading magazines. These titles included ImagineFX, 3D World and video game titles Play and Official PlayStation Magazine. Ian launched Xbox magazine X360 and edited PlayStation World. For Creative Bloq, Ian combines his experiences to bring the latest news on digital art, VFX and video games and tech, and in his spare time he doodles in Procreate, ArtRage, and Rebelle while finding time to play Xbox and PS5.

items.title: The best Christmas gifts in the UK for dads, grandads, uncles and friends – tested for 2026
paragraphs: Gifts for dads, grandads and other father figures can often feel like a shot in the dark. What do you get for someone who doesn’t seem to want anything, or who already has it all?
Shared experiences or promises of peace and quiet are popular options, but they are tricky to wrap. Which is where my recommendations come in.

Each gift I’ve featured has been put through its paces by me for the past few months and has made it into this list because it has become something I reach for on a near-daily basis (or, in the case of the AeroPress coffee maker, multiple times a day).

Testing has involved cooking copious amounts of rice, making my home smell like a greenhouse and rolling my sleeves up in the garden (and I don’t think I’ll need to sharpen my knives for a while). So rest assured, my suggestions have the approval of at least one 34-year-old dad with a toddler (me).

Despite the rise in Apple Pay and its Android equivalent, wallets still have their place in a pocket. This neat design from Roka London has three interior compartments for cards, coins and receipts. Made from a durable recycled canvas, it has retained its good looks after months of cut-and-thrust testing, and kept its contents dry in a downpour when my trousers weren’t as lucky.

A water bottle should last longer if it’s easy to clean, and Chilly’s latest even comes with a telescopic brush to make keeping on top of seals and its stainless steel straw a cinch. It’s leak-free and promises to keep its contents cold for a whole working day (and beyond – Chilly’s says up to 45 hours), while the flip lid allows for one-handed drinking on the go. It ticks all the water bottle boxes.
For more, read the Filter’s guide to the best water bottles

Personalised gifts can be hit and miss, but this high-quality print from Good Team On Paper falls firmly in the former camp. The company will design a poster based on the memorable kits of any team (from non-league to national sides), and the result is a tasteful piece of art that is a cut above most sporting merch. My Arsenal-mad brother confirmed the early 90s yellow and black JVC away shirt was a particularly accurate representation.

Don’t be fooled by its colour. This spade might scream bling, but it’s an invaluable addition to any garden shed. It can break up rock-solid borders in no time, and its sharp tip has been great for dividing perennials.
Tomato vine refillable candle starter pack

Brighten up any WFH setting with a candle from Pott. Its collaboration with Isle of Wight Tomatoes is a welcome change from traditional scents and has brought a deep, summery tomato vine smell to my office as the nights have drawn in. Its jazzy pot can be used again with a candle refill, making it a longstanding staple of any desk.

Electronics and outdoorsy dads don’t always mix well, but this portable speaker from Ultimate Ears is up to the challenge, including being submerged in water (it has an IP67 rating) and getting dropped in the sand by my toddler during a day trip to the beach. Its sound quality is surprisingly strong and bassy for such a small package (10.4cm high), and the audio doesn’t break up when cranked to the max.

An earplug is an essential part of my sleep routine, though they rarely stay in until the morning. Happy Ears solved this issue with this discovery pack, helping me find a size that fits. Rather than completely blocking noise, they take an ambient edge off, and their use isn’t limited to the bedroom: they’ve been great for swimming and help at gigs, too.

Although on the small side, this wash bag seems Tardis-like and has managed to fit all the essentials for weekends away and longer stays without taking up loads of room in luggage. Its zipped compartment means you don’t have to rummage for small items like contact lens cases and tweezers, and its integrated hanging loop was helpful when sink space was at a minimum.

Swap out the plastic pump bottle for this face cleansing bar from Lifejacket. The bar itself lasted about three months of daily use and left my face feeling clear, refreshed and ready for bed after a day of sweat from exercising.

For time-poor dads who aren’t au fait with a solid skincare routine, a moisturiser keeps things simple while soothing dry skin. This pick from French brand Horace packs SPF30 coverage, a matte finish with no glossy sheen, and instant absorption so it takes seconds to apply.
For more, read our guide to the best face moisturisers

This refillable applicator and bar set from Bob lets you ditch the plastic bottle of shower gel. The applicator’s bristles help get a real lather going, and the bars themselves leave skin feeling clean and smelling subtly of peppermint and lime for the rest of the day.

An AeroPress is the gateway method to making great coffee at home. Relatively mess-free, simple to clean and a fraction of the size of an espresso machine, I have used one daily for more than 10 years.
For more, read our guide to the best coffee machines for every home and budget

Sharp knives are safe knives – a blunt blade is more likely to slip – and this neat tool from Joseph Joseph has become a great, compact addition to my cutlery drawer. Dull, old knives have been given new life with some swipes on the coarse and fine ceramic sharpening wheels; its non-slip feet mean it feels secure to use.
For more, read our guide on how to look after your kitchen knives

Substitute his scratched non-stick and its microplastic particles for stainless steel. I’ve found this tri-ply frying pan brilliant for steaks, stir-fries, scrambled eggs; its high sides mean it can even work for stews. Plus, it will survive contact with metal implements and over-enthusiastic scrubbing.
For more, read our guide to the best frying pans

Sichuan peppercorns are something of an acquired taste, but if you’re buying for a fan of the mouth-numbing spice, this chilli crisp lingers on the tongue and lips. Great in stir-fries, dolloped on dumplings or slathered on scrambled eggs, it adds a tingly sensation to any dish.

Cold brew isn’t just for summer: this Hario glass brewer is a feature of my fridge long into the depths of winter. The simplicity of brewing is the big draw – stick ground coffee and cold water in before bed and wake to a beautifully balanced cup. Having a batch to hand means it can also be used for cocktails such as carajillo and espresso martini without a coffee machine.

Spending more than £100 on a knife may seem excessive, but this 8in Wüsthof chef’s knife has left the rest of my block firmly in the shade. Its handle has a satisfying weight that keeps you in control, while the blade is remarkably sharp and adept at everything from deboning chicken thighs to finely chopping garlic.
For more, read our guide to the best (and worst) chef’s knives

The Rambler is a rock-solid reusable cup from outdoor specialist Yeti, and its cup-holder compatibility makes it ideal for dad’s taxi. For an extra £8, it’s possible to add a personalised message to create a unique gift for your one-of-a-kind.
For more, read our guide to the best travel mugs
Bruichladdich the classic laddie whisky, 70cl

A contemporary take on a classic, this 10-year-aged single malt scotch is an approachable drop with a sweet nose and warming, biscuity taste that should get the seal of approval from aficionados and newcomers alike.
For more, read our guide to the best whisky

This infuser makes brewing a mug of loose leaf tea straightforward. Fill with tea, plonk in a mug, pour over water and hey presto, you’ve got the taste of a teapot without the big clean-up operation and the convenience of a teabag minus the microplastics.

A hot drink instantly tastes better when it’s served in posh crockery, and Villa Bologna’s handmade and handpainted striped number has an artisan feel without the associated price. Dishwasher safe and able to hold 400ml of tea or coffee, it’s a serious upgrade on his faded Sports Direct mug.

Whether drenched on tofu, stir-fries and rice, or used as a marinade for chicken or salmon, this Korean soy and garlic barbecue sauce was an instant hit in my household. It’s moreish … so won’t last long.

Negroni’s three ingredients – gin, Campari and vermouth – make it one of the most straightforward cocktails to create, but not all serves are made equal. Black Lines’ premixed concoction is better than most, and means aperitivo hour is only the uncorking of a bottle away.

Gluten-free, vegan and carbon-negative, Jiddler’s Tipple craft beer creations are as guilt-free as they come. Its hoppy core range – which is included in this gift set with a vintage shirt pattern-inspired pint glass – all sit under 3.8% ABV too, so are less likely to leave a headache the next morning.

Low-alcohol doesn’t have to be boring, as this Rothaus brew proves. After sampling a pint of the crisp, smooth 0.4% wheat beer in the summer, I was thrilled to find it came in a bottle for sober sipping at home. The flavour profile is perfect for the festive period, but also a welcome treat in warmer weather.
Forest Feast dark chocolate cashews, 120g

Swerve the chocolate orange stocking filler this year for a packet of these Belgian chocolate-covered salted cashews instead. A luxurious taste that perfectly balances the bitterness of dark chocolate with a hit of salt; buy a pack for yourself too, as they won’t be offered around.
Vina Real Rioja Gran Reserva Especial 2018, 75cl

If your old man knows his way around the wine aisle, then this special rioja is a sure-fire hit. A 2018 vintage that won’t break the bank, it has fruity notes that go well with red meat or manchego. Its ageing potential means it will also be a welcome addition to any burgeoning cellar (if it makes it through the festive period).

This rice cooker has become an invaluable addition to my kitchen, and a gadget that earns its place on a limited work surface. It’s simple to use – add water and rinsed rice, select the type (white, brown or short grain) – and about 40 minutes later you’re left with fluffy individual grains with no effort. For big families, Yum Asia’s Sakura has a larger capacity and can make up to 16 portions of rice in one go.
For more, read our guide to the best rice cookers

A great stocking filler for the parkrun-obsessed pops, these socks from Hoka have a plush, cushioned feel underfoot when pounding the streets. They stay firmly in place even if you pick up the pace courtesy of an anti-slip silicone strip on the ball of the foot.

A base layer with fashion credentials, this moisture-wicking short-sleeve from Nike subbrand ACG keeps things cool during a run but won’t look out of place when they’re not working out. A slightly thicker front panel keeps the chill off on colder starts while mesh panels at the rear and armpits handle hotspots with ease.

A fleece for all occasions, this versatile pullover from Arc’teryx has been a brilliant addition to my wardrobe. The organic cotton has a soft touch against bare skin and is great for lazy days around the house. But it’s equally adept when heading out in the cold for a walk or layering as part of a smarter get-up.

This has become a firm fixture on my cookbook stand, filled with quick fresh recipes that make veg, beans and vegan protein such as tofu sing – from fast-assembly jobs like the WFH-friendly store-cupboard bean salad to the hearty lentil cottage pie that will have him converted from the beef version.
The Things We Never Say by Elizabeth Strout

Elizabeth Strout’s Booker prize-shortlisted novel has a father as its focus and deals with themes inside and outside the home through protagonist Artie Dam’s lens. Funny, sad and at times a real thinker, it’s a refreshing break for anyone caught in the thriller loop.

An engrossing nonfiction read with the mysterious death of a young man as its focal point, Patrick Radden Keefe’s bestseller is a page-turner that sheds light on London’s dark underbelly, complete with lies, deceit and dirty money.

Warm and luxurious, the recycled polyester fleece hooded dressing gown from Chelsea Peers belies its price. It’s the first thing I reach for in the morning and has even stayed on deep into the afternoon on those video-call-free work-from-home days.

Darn Tough is known for its hiking socks, but I feel its lifestyle lineup is a step above any high-street hosiery. Despite their lightweight construction, the cushioning is the sort of support you expect from thicker walking socks, while the merino wool adds warmth in winter without getting sweaty on hotter days.
Comfortable in a wide range of temperatures and showing no signs of wear after several washes, these posh pyjama bottoms are worth the expense, and you won’t need to replace them in 12 months.

Slippers are a Christmas gift staple, but these suede M&S mules are an upgrade on any run-of-the-mill moccasins. The shearling lining gives your feet a cosy cuddle, and an antibacterial treatment keeps them smelling fresh, despite hours of wear.

This soft, stylish beanie from Cornwall-based B Corp Finisterre is minimalist in design and made from merino wool. It keeps the warmth in and the cold at bay without blocking my ears, making it great for ear pod use or staying alert for any impending toddler tantrums.

Brewery merch can often be naff, but this collaboration between Guinness and Manchester-based UN:IK is a legitimate addition to any T-shirt drawer. It pairs the Irish stout’s classic posters with a washed-out design and is a great gift for any G-splitting pros.

This small-batch extra virgin olive oil subscription is ideal for foodies who want to add punch to a dish – whether it’s salads, pasta or drizzled on Greek yoghurt. Handpicked and cold pressed in Crete, two bottles come directly from the farmers every two or three months, and for £30 a pop it beats supermarket fodder hands down on taste, price and sustainability.
Workshop Coffee subscription, three months

For adventurous types who are happy to have their taste buds tested, the Workshop single-origin coffee subscription offers a rotating selection of roasts. Available for filter or espresso brewing and as whole beans or ground for various brewing methods, a new brew arrives through the letterbox each month, and can be as varied as a lightly roasted zesty Ethiopian and a dark and deep Colombian cup.
National Trust individual membership, one year

Although you might have to get creative with your presentation of this gift (time to fire up Canva and dust down the printer), for less than two pints of beer a month (£8.40), you can provide free entry (and parking at most properties) to more than 500 National Trust sites around England, Wales and Northern Ireland (with some access to Scottish sites). Whether it’s interesting family days out, short solo walks around some grounds, or interesting ways to break up a long car journey, this pass will have you covered.
For more, read our guide to the best Christmas gifts for mums, grannies, aunties and friends and the best reusable Christmas decorations

Christmas shopping can be tough, but the Filter is here to help. We’ve been testing Christmas presents all year to help you find thoughtful, creative and genuinely brilliant gifts for everyone on your list. Browse our other gift guides for hundreds more tried-and-tested ideas, from gifts you can make yourself to toys for every age group.

Charlie Allenby is a health and fitness journalist who also became a parent in 2024, meaning he juggles testing gear around nap times (or combines the two with his trusty running buggy). He has always enjoyed going the extra mile when it comes to sourcing gifts, keeping a phone note that he updates as soon as he has an idea for various loved ones

items.title: Dior's Christmas ad is the opposite to Prada's classy animation
paragraphs: The 2026 Christmas advert season is here, but with so many brands throwing their hat in the ring, standing out requires some real ingenuity. This year, brands have embraced a handcrafted approach, like Levi's stunning stop-motion film and Prada's Disney-inspired ad, but it seems there's an imposter among the ranks.

Dior's latest holiday ad has been lambasted for allegedly using AI-generated content, disguised as the work of human craft. While the best Christmas adverts don't follow a formula, Dior's 'animated' ad appears to be stolen valour, proving that audiences are hungry for authenticity when it comes to advertising.
“Christian Dior’s Night in Color” - YouTube

Directed by French animator Sylvain Chomet, “Christian Dior’s Night in Color,” is (on the surface) a charming short film inspired by the founder's friendship with film star Marlene Dietrich. With an all-star cast including Robert Pattinson, Rihanna, Josh O’Connor and LaKeith Stanfield, the ad captures a familiar festive warmth, supported by its seemingly hand-illustrated animation.
watching "christian dior's night in color" and.... am i the only one noticing this is ai? https://t.co/7QEHjFtAMMNovember 4, 2026
But soon eagle-eyed viewers spotted some subtle discrepancies. Strange warped lettering, a lazy eye here, a misplaced phalange there – all signs seemed to point to AI slop.

But it was not the alleged AI that irked critics so much; it was the deception. A 'behind-the-scenes' look at production shows only sketches, and as the end credits roll, a short list of animators are listed with no mention of AI, (despite evidence suggesting otherwise). Paired with Chomet's creative legacy, Dior's intentions become clear – it wants you to believe this is 100% human animation.

Comments were suitably heated, with one X user writing "Your budget couldn't fit in an actual animation studio? You had to use AI? Disappointing." Another added "After the Prada commercial, its so easy to see its AI. Its so sad to see many good artists put their names behind this," while another added, "Oh Dior can rot in a ditch for not disclosing they resorted to ai-slop. All these 'pretty' visuals mean nothing if no artist animated them."

During this year's Christmas ad season, human-made craft has become synonymous with nostalgia and luxury – praiseworthy traits that earn brand's the audience seal of approval. Dior's sly attempt to capitalise on this trend has only peeved critics further, proving that even the most subtle AI blemishes will be called out. While Dior's AI augmentation is merely speculation, the brand's lack of transparency only aids in audience mistrust and frustration.
For more advertising news, check out the reaction to John Lewis' new Christmas ad or take a look at the most beautiful Christmas films to inspire you this festive season.

Natalie Fear is Creative Bloq's staff writer. With an eye for trending topics and a passion for internet culture, she brings you the latest in art and design news. Natalie also runs Creative Bloq’s 5 Questions series, spotlighting diverse talent across the creative industries. Outside of work, she loves all things literature and music (although she’s partial to a spot of TikTok brain rot).

items.title: Investigation into 'major fish kill' after pollution incident
paragraphs: The angling club said that the pollution incident killed brown and migratory sea trout
A investigation is underway after "a major fish kill" in a County Down river, the Department for Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (Daera) has confirmed.
The pollution caused the death of brown and migratory sea trout in the Gransha, Ballystockart and Inler (also known as Enler) Rivers.
Glenn McKibbin, the secretary of Inler Angling Club, said about 1,000 fish were killed in the incident and it "could not have happened in a worse location on the river or at a worse time".
The Northern Ireland Environment Agency (NIEA) and Daera Inland Fisheries are working to "identify the source of the pollution and to finalise the numbers of fish killed".
The Department said the incident was reported by a member of the public on Tuesday at 09:30 GMT.
The club said that the fish killing impacts resident kingfishers, herons and otters
McKibbin said that "current and future fish stocks obliterated for years to come".
He added that resident and non-resident migratory fish, which only return at this of year to spawn, have been impacted.
"Knock-on effects for other wildlife such as resident kingfishers, herons & otters unavoidable.

"For our members and volunteers who work tirelessly in a bid to improve the river this is soul-destroying, particularly as the river was still in recovery from major pollution incidents / fish kills in 2013 and 2015," McKibbin said.
"Waterways up and down the country continue to be treated like sewers.
"The paltry fines that usually follow incidents of this nature are not a deterrent and the current 'system' is broken."
Many migratory fish, such as trout and salmon, swim up smaller tributaries to lay their eggs in cleaner, gravel-bottomed, or cooler waters away from larger predators in the main river.
A tributary is a smaller river that flows into a larger mainstem river where many migratory fish, such as trout and salmon, swim up to lay their eggs away from larger predators in the main river.

Inler Angling Club Chairperson David Pyper said: "For those who dedicate so much time and effort to caring for the river, witnessing the sheer loss of fish in circumstances such as these is particularly disappointing.
"The club hopes that the forthcoming investigations will establish the cause of this latest incident and help ensure appropriate steps are taken to protect the river and its wildlife."
The club has encouraged local representatives and authorities to continue to prioritise rivers and direct resources towards improving water quality and preventing further incidents.

items.title: The Russell Brand I saw in court was not the flamboyant character most people will know
paragraphs: In the dock Brand's statue-like demeanour was broken only occasionally, when, during some of the evidence, he closed his eyes for several seconds, perhaps in silent prayer or meditation. There was no fidgeting or movement. He didn't flinch.

He maintained his composure even during some of the most harrowing evidence, when one of the victims told the court how blood and faeces had been left on Brand's bed sheets after he had raped her at his house.
During the testimony, Brand let out a sigh and looked at the ceiling with his eyes closed.
Speculation grew about whether Brand would give evidence - defendants can choose whether to take to the stand in their trials. It became a daily talking point among the reporters.
Giving evidence yourself can be a double-edged sword; a chance to vigorously defend one's innocence on the one hand, balanced by the risk of being torn apart by the prosecution barrister.

But it finally happened. Brand took to the witness box on day 10 of the trial. His testimony was perhaps unsurprising - after all, nobody apart from his wife had been prepared to speak up for him in court as part of the defence's case.

Brand entered the witness box wearing a dark suit and a white open-necked shirt. It was a nervous beginning. In an unusually loud voice he answered "no" to each of the allegations that were put to him.
He had taken his bible oath loudly too and stood, bolt upright with hands clasped behind his back.
I watched him like a hawk. This was a TV personality who was very much part of my youth, but now being interrogated with his liberty on the line.

His nerves seemed to visibly ease, so much so that at one point he put his hands in his pockets. It was noticeable that after an adjournment, he was back in his ramrod style stance with hands out of his pockets, behind his back.
His wife attended court with him every day - soberly dressed, she sometimes took notes when the complainants were giving evidence.
Her support for her husband was visible - holding his hand as they walked in, smiling at him while he was in the dock for hours at a time.

Brand's minder often sat next to her in the public benches, and her father, former Ryder Cup-winning golfer Bernard Gallacher sat with her in the gallery during the defence closing. Brand's father, Ron, also attended regularly, exchanging polite chat with some of the media.

At 51 years of age, Brand looked gaunt and visibly thinner as the trial neared its end, he seemed to have lost weight as the days went on. Other reporters said the same. We discussed whether signs of confidence he showed at the start had slowly ebbed away.
The verdicts came on Thursday after the jury had been deliberating for eight hours and 30 minutes.
Brand, who stood upright in the dock, showed limited emotion as the verdicts were read out. "Sit down Mr Brand," the judge told him after the verdicts were delivered.
"On what happens next," he added, "obviously a custodial sentence of some length will result."
Brand mouthed "I'm good, I'm good" to his defence counsel as he was led away.
But his appearance in court was an extraordinary fall from grace. A man hailed as a multi-media celebrity, a self-confessed ladies' man too, but now a convicted rapist in custody.

items.title: Nvidia DLSS 5 AI in Hogwarts Legacy is the opposite of what everyone expected
paragraphs: As if Potterheads didn't have enough to worry about amid the controversy around the design changes in HBO's Harry Potter series, Hogwarts Legacy now has Nvidia DLSS 5 enhancements. The next generation of Nvidia's AI-driven neural rendering and upscaling came to the game today, and those following the backlash over the tech were prepared for the worst.

So does DLSS 5 ride roughshod over Hogwarts Legacy's art direction and create entirely new characters like people expected when the leaked unfinished DLSS 5 iteration surfaced online back in August? Erm...
Hogwarts Legacy | DLSS 5 Launch Trailer - YouTube

As demonstrated by Nvidia in the launch trailer above, the impact of DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy looks surprisingly subtle. The chip giant maintains that the aim is to enhance lighting and material quality to "boost environmental uplift while preserving character identity".

"With the addition of DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering to Hogwarts Legacy, our complete suite of DLSS technologies will now be supported, enabling you to accelerate and enhance your experiences in the wizarding world," Nvidia says.

It seems it just can't please people. After the ridicule Nvidia faced for the initial tests of DLSS 5, some people are now saying that the actual implementation in Hogwarts Legacy is laughably subtle. Some are struggling to see a worthwhile difference even in side-by-side comparisons "Before vs Before", one person jokes in the comments on the trailer above.
What do you think of the comparisons below?
"People complained too much that they just completely nerfed it. Now we just have fps loss with basically little difference in image quality," one person complains in the comments on YouTube.

"I find it hilarious how the first presentation was so completely over the top strength wise, and now it's reduced to a point where you really can't even tell if it's even on anymore without a direct comparison," someone else writes.
"Asking for another 100-200 watts of power for basically no difference is crazy work," a third person suggests.

Alas, the relatively subtle implementation is unlikely to end the DLSS 5 controversy. While some scenes arguably benefit from a subtle boost in contrast, the extra detail in some of the environments actually makes them feel less atmospheric in my opinion.

Official DLSS 5 support is currently limited to GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs and RTX Spark systems. Activating DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, 6X Multi Frame Generation, Ray Reconstruction, NVIDIA Reflex, and ray tracing, allows Hogwarts Legacy to run at a max of 4K at up to 300 frames per second on RTX 5090 (see our guide the best GPUs).

"For an optimal experience, we also recommend enabling DLSS Super Resolution under 'Upscale Type', DLSS Multi Frame Generation under 'Frame Generation', NVIDIA Reflex under 'Low Latency Mode', and 'DLSS Ray Reconstruction' if you're also activating Hogwarts Legacy's immersive ray-traced effects," Nvidia adds.

DLSS 5 is also coming to the free-to-play military combat game War Thunder from mid-November and to the wuxia-inspired Where Winds Meet from 23 November. You can read the full blog post on the Nvidia website

Nvidia said back in March that its next-generation DLSS would bring "photorealism" to gaming through the use of a new generative AI model designed to enhance frames and add detail to lighting, textures and materials in real time. But the GPU maker's early demo immediately sparked controversy by giving Grace from Capcom’s Resident Evil Requiem a glamour makeover.

Leaked through the nvngx_dlssnr.dll library via NBA 2K27, modders soon began testing DLSS 5 for themselves and sharing the videos and screenshots on social media. Faces were the main area of contention, with some modders complaining that Nvidia's new tech makes characters look uncanny and AI-generated or older than they're supposed to be by sharpening skin texture.
That sparked a big debate around artistic intent, with some people concerned that the technology would effectively change game artists' original vision.

items.title: A bull in a car – level 1
paragraphs: Something crazy happens in Norfolk, the United States. People see a big bull in the back of a car.
The driver’s name is Lee Meyer. He makes some changes to his car. The bull fits in the car thanks to the changes. People, who see the car, call the police. The police stop the car.

The bull is a big Watsui bull. This bull has really big horns. The police explain the driver that the situation is dangerous. An accident may happen. The bull’s name is Howdy Doody. Reports do not say where the man and the bull are going.
Difficult words: fit (to be small enough to stay in a place), horn (a hard part on an animal’s head), explain (to make something clear).
You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: A bull in a car – level 2
paragraphs: In Norfolk, the United States, the police responded to reports of a man driving with a cow in his car.

When they stopped the car, they were surprised to find a massive Watusi bull as the passenger. The police issued the driver a warning due to the unusual situation, which could possibly cause an accident. The bull’s name was Howdy Doody, and the driver had to make some changes in his car to fit the bull in. This incident attracted attention from onlookers who called the police. It’s unclear where the bull and the driver were going.
Difficult words: massive (very big), attention (when people are interested in something), onlooker (a person who sees something happen).
You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: A bull in a car – level 3
paragraphs: In Norfolk, the United States, police were surprised when they received reports of a man driving with a cow in his car, only to discover a massive Watusi bull as the passenger.

This breed of African cattle is known for its gigantic horns. The driver, Lee Meyer, was stopped by the police, who issued him a warning due to the unusual and potentially unsafe situation. The bull named Howdy Doody could only fit in the car after modifications were made, including removing parts of the car’s body and windshield and installing a platform.
The incident drew attention from onlookers, and it’s unclear where the bull and the driver were heading.
Difficult words: breed (a particular type of animal or plant), modification (change), windshield (a window at the front of a car).
